answer: Stop when the favorable latency is not a decision-grade measurement, and report INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (or MEASURE_FIRST / REJECTED_BY_GATE) instead of an architecture conclusion. The stopping conditions are: (1) the apparent gain is within documented measurement noise, variance is high, samples are too few, or trials are not repeated; (2) the test did not deliver the intended demand - a saturated or closed-loop generator suppresses offered load, or the latency figure counts only completed requests and omits timed-out, rejected, cancelled or unsent intended operations; (3) baseline and candidate were not compared at equivalent offered demand and resource budget, or differed in application/data revision, runtime/configuration or warm/cold state, so lower latency may be a capacity purchase or missing work; (4) a hard gate fails (correctness, authorization, consistency, durable state, compatibility or recovery) or an unsafe abort condition is reached; (5) the decision threshold was chosen or changed after seeing the result (peeking, threshold shopping, or summarizing a heavy tail by its mean). In these cases the experiment has reached its stopping condition: record the narrowest next source, measurement or owner decision, repair the experiment, and rerun with a pre-registered criterion at equal demand and resource budget. Do not generalize a favorable p99 from one run into proof of an architecture improvement.
